correctness.rationale: For Haar-almost-every normal, section vertices correspond bijectively to box-edge transversal crossings; there are \(2^{d-1}\) edges per coordinate axis. The crossing inequality compares independent centered Gaussians with variances \(a_i^2\) and \(\sum_{j\ne i}a_j^2\); the Cauchy ratio distribution gives crossing probability \(\frac2\pi\arcsin(a_i/\sqrt{\sum_j a_j^2})\). Summing indicators yields the exact formula. Strict Schur monotonicity follows because the derivative of \(f(t)=\arcsin\sqrt t\) is \(1/(2\sqrt{t(1-t)})\) and the pair-difference product \((x-y)(1-x-y)\) is positive when a third probability coordinate is positive. Merging coordinates bounds the arcsine sum strictly below by \(\pi/2\) for positive vectors in dimensions at least three, and continuity proves the sharp infimum. The uniform extremum and local Taylor coefficient follow exactly; the four-dimensional cube mean is \(32/3\). The standalone verifier independently counted all coordinate-edge crossings at finite Gaussian samples and checked transfers and local derivatives. Sampling is not used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The exact Haar-centered orthotope expectation and strict squared-side-length Schur concavity for \(d\ge4\) were compared by mathematical implication against the source on translated random cube slices, the source on central cube sectional volumes, Ball–Prodromou’s unrelated combinatorial isotropy theorem, the 2015 central-model question and random-cone face count formulas. All plausible full texts available were read. Swan fixes a different probability distribution and thus cannot imply the anisotropic central law; neither the 2008 volume formulas nor random-cone results give it. The dimension-three axial special case available from previously published shadow probabilities is not claimed as new. Broad search failure does not establish novelty absolutely; risks are recorded.
residual_risks: An earlier derivation of the simple Gaussian–Cauchy crossing probability or the arcsine majorization inequality may exist under different terminology or in a book.

No independent mathematical review or comprehensive survey of all international literature has been performed.

value.rationale: The expected combinatorial complexity of Haar-random central sections of a canonical box family is a natural, previously separated random-section observable (explicitly considered as a model in a 2015 public question), not an arbitrary parameter slice. The theorem supplies the complete exact dimension-independent functional on all positive orthotopes, proves counterintuitive strict Schur-concavity despite scalar arcsine-sqrt changing convexity, classifies the unique maximum, determines the nonattained sharp lower infimum and a nonzero stability Hessian, and gives the exact four-dimensional benchmark \(32/3\). It exposes the substantive distinction between center-pinned and uniformly translated slicing, in which the latter has the constant mean \(2^{d-1}\). These implications are mathematically meaningful without a paper-sized downstream theorem.
